rationale: C15 plausibly supplied a major, concrete drafting template for the child. The child revises the same Part 1655 provisions established by C15—§§ 1655.2, 1655.4, 1655.5, and 1655.6—while preserving their sequence, administrative machinery, forms, jurisdictional rule, and extensive language, chiefly updating the geographic terminology after Alaska and Hawaii became States. C07 and C12 also contain near-verbatim antecedents for other child provisions, but C15 contributes the broadest coherent block.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Unless he is a person excepted from registration by section 6(a) ... every male citizen of the United States outside the continental United States, the State of Alaska, the State of Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, and the Canal Zone ... is required ... to present himself for and submit to registration before (1) any diplomatic or consular officer ... (2) any other person ... appointed ... as chief registrar; or (3) any registrar appointed as provided in § 1655.3.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Unless he is a person excepted from registration by section 6(a) ... every male citizen of the United States outside of the several States of the United States, the District of Columbia, the Territory of Alaska, the Territory of Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the virgin Islands, Guam, and the Canal Zone ... shall ... present himself for and submit to registration before—(1) Any diplomatic or consular officer ... (2) Any other person ... appointed ... as chief registrar; or (3) Any registrar appointed as provided in § 1655.3.
shared_material.explanation: The child retains C15's distinctive registration rule, age framework, three-part registrar list, and statutory machinery while updating geographic and temporal wording.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Each such person who is registered shall designate for entry on line 2 of his Registration Questionnaire—Foreign (SSS Form No. 50) the address of his place of residence within the continental United States, the State of Alaska, the State of Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, or the Canal Zone ... If any such person fails or refuses ... jurisdiction over him ... shall vest in District of Columbia Local Board No. 100 (Foreign).
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Each such person who is registered shall designate for entry on line 2 of his Registration Questionnaire-Foreign (SSS Form No. 50) the address of his place of residence within any of the several States ... the Territory of Alaska, the Territory of Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, or the Canal Zone ... If any such person fails or refuses ... jurisdiction over him ... shall vest in District of Columbia Local Board No. 100 (Foreign).
shared_material.explanation: This is an unusually specific administrative mechanism reproduced nearly verbatim, including the same form, line number, fallback designation, and special local-board jurisdiction.

shared_material.child_excerpt: District of Columbia Local Board No. 100 (Foreign) shall have jurisdiction for all purposes under the selective service law over any person who at the time of his registration ... does not designate for entry on line 2 of his Registration Questionnaire—Foreign (SSS Form No. 50) an address of a place within the continental United States, the State of Alaska, the State of Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, or the Canal Zone.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: District of Columbia Local Board No. 100 (Foreign) shall have jurisdiction for all purposes under the selective service law over any person who at the time of his registration ... does not designate for entry on line 2 of his Registration Questionnaire-Foreign (SSS Form No. 50) an address of a place within any of the several States ... the Territory of Alaska, the Territory of Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, Guam, or the Canal Zone.
shared_material.explanation: The same specialized jurisdictional provision and drafting structure are retained with geographic-status substitutions.
